headline: Strong India and developed markets offset US erosion; FY28 to remain a transition year

highlights: Strong India momentum and pipeline opportunities are offset by limited near-term US earnings visibility and margin recovery.

Business performance: Lupin’s revenue grew 11.1% YoY to Rs78.3bn, led by India (+14.7% to Rs23.8bn), other developed markets (+45.7% to Rs11.8bn; Europe, Australia, and Canada, with Europe delivering double-digit growth even ex-VISUfarma), and API (+20.2% to Rs3.1bn).

US revenue grew 9.3% to Rs30.2bn, but was nearly flat in dollar terms at US$317mn (+0.2%), as higher base volumes and seasonal demand were offset by tolvaptan pricing pressure following two additional generic entrants.
EBITDA fell 8.4% to Rs19.6bn, with margins contracting by 532bps to 25.0%, owing to US price erosion, higher employee and field costs, settlement-linked licence fees, and increased R&D.
valuation: Valuation: We maintain our HOLD rating with a revised target price of Rs2,144 (earlier: Rs2,669), derived by rolling forward our valuation to Sep-28E and applying 25x FY28E EPS.

The lower target price reflects the moderation in our earnings estimates, with FY28 expected to be a transition year as intensifying competition and erosion in key US products weigh on profitability, while elevated R&D and commercialisation investments constrain operating leverage.
Launch is planned for Q1FY28, targeting select channels rather than a direct-to-consumer play.
watch: Outlook: We estimate revenue of Rs306.2bn, Rs313.3bn, and Rs336.3bn in FY27E, FY28E, and FY29E, respectively.
India will remain the key growth driver, supported by the management's guidance of 1.2-1.3x IPM growth and increasing chronic contribution.
